evidence: STRUCTURE (source review; no structural inversion found). (1) tests/scoring.toml:1-11 sets gates render/constraints 0.0, weights functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2 and a functional floor of 0.05. It is byte-identical to the template scoring.toml and score.py (diff clean). In score.py:41-48 any gate failure or functional<=0.05 gives reward 0; otherwise reward is the linear weighted mean of dimensions in [0,1]. Reward never decreases when a dimension score rises, so the aggregation cannot invert a ranking. Function outweighs craft (0.6 vs 0.4). The polish dimension here grades behaviour under concurrency (live-update preservation, keeping the place when paging, failed send, session resume), so pure visual craft is only 0.2. (2) Floor vs criterion granularity: the functional weights 4.5+7+4+5.5+5+7+4+4.5+6+5.5+3.5+4.5 sum to 61, matching the comment at functional/judge.toml:23. The smallest criterion (hro_unread_seen, 3.5) is 3.5/61 = 0.057 > 0.05, so passing any one functional criterion clears the floor. No cliff floors an app with more functional credit while a weaker one clears it. (3) The gates stay simple, as Colderwater lesson 4 asks. The render gate (gates/render/judge.toml:25) refuses a wrong password, and the correct sign-in shows a usable workspace. The constraints gate (gates/constraints/judge.toml:25) adds a candidate through the UI, checks that a reload keeps the user signed in, and has the Observer read the card in an independent context. Every condition is in the public brief: instruction.md:7 treats a reload differently from being signed out, and hireops_rules.md:17-19 says Recruiters add candidates and the Observer reads the board. I found no gate that a stronger conforming app would fail while a weaker one passes. Both gates are all_pass binary, weight 1, with zero reward mass. (4) Dead features cannot earn credit, which would invert ranking. functional/prompt.md:17 requires a same-session positive control for every refusal leg. hro_readonly_roles (functional/judge.toml:94) leaves out kinds whose staff control never succeeded and scores 0 if none succeeded. hro_candidate (:130) scores 0 if the candidate page receives none of its own data. hro_two_people (:49) uses the original move as the control. The polish live rows hro_pol_live_board and hro_pol_live_thread score 0 if no update arrives within 60 s. hro_pol_failed_send and hro_pol_session_resume each need a successful re-send. visual/prompt.md:12 gives a gate-failing shell Likert 1, which normalises to 0. (5) Conforming alternatives are accepted, so a better product is not penalised. hro_interview_places (:58) accepts three UIs: optimistic move with rollback, refusal before the move, and a move that is not offered but shows the reason. hro_readonly_roles (:94) and hro_messaging (:103) leave the visibility of write controls to the app. functional/prompt.md:21 lets a leg blocked by another criterion's broken feature be judged on the state the app actually produced, so it is not failed twice. (6) Colderwater lesson 16 (double grading): arrival speed is graded only in Functional and preservation only in Polish, and the polish rows say so. An app with no live updates loses the functional legs and the polish live rows. That amplifies the penalty but does not invert the ranking. (7) Colderwater lesson 2 (equal-weight recompute): the weights follow one documented scheme, with legs weighted 1.0/1.5/2.0 and summed per individual-session criterion. Each criterion is binary and the aggregation linear, so an equal-weight recompute changes the magnitudes but not the direction of any criterion. The weight scheme causes no inversion. NOTES (not proven defects; reasons for risk=true). (a) Required runtime evidence is missing. The scope field of raw-evidence-index.json says 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent.' The only runtime evidence is the scripted golden driver (via-solve.log: 26 groups PASS, hashes verified). It is not a judge run and says nothing about how weak or mutated apps rank against the golden. REVIEW_POLICY.md ('Runtime and model evidence') requires a hash-bound reward-ordering record, and the workbook's internal note on this row ('we need to monitor this one') also asks for a measured check. Monotonicity therefore cannot be upgraded to Pass. (b) Template-policy note (not a task defect; must not be edited). Under the frozen 0.6/0.2/0.2 weights and 0.05 floor, an app that passes one small functional criterion (0.057) with full visual and polish scores about 0.43. That is above an app with functional 0.6 and zero polish and visual (0.36). In practice, full polish requires working live updates, paging and drafts, so such an app would also earn more functional credit. This is recorded only for the monitoring the workbook asks for. (c) P3 latent risk to a conforming alternative. The brief lets the builder keep drafts anywhere (hireops_rules.md:176-181, 'Where drafts are kept is up to you'). Step (3) of hro_messaging (functional/judge.toml:103) leaves an unsent reply in 'another conversation'. Later, hro_long_thread (:112) types an unfinished reply in Noor's Platform Engineer conversation and requires that 'the reply still reads exactly what was typed'. An app that keeps drafts server-side per person would correctly restore an earlier leftover draft there, and so would any setup where the browser profile survives between individual sessions. A literal judge could then fail hro_long_thread (5.5) for correct behaviour that an app without drafts would never trigger. The polish prompt handles this case (polish/prompt.md:14: 'If a message or note box already holds text from an earlier review, record it and clear it'), but functional/prompt.md has no such line. The golden keeps drafts in browser storage (threads.js:113,125,183,197) and the Playwright MCP launches with --isolated, so the golden is probably unaffected, but this is unmeasured. The app without drafts also fails hro_messaging (6) and hro_pol_session_resume, so the overall ranking is unlikely to invert. This is why it is a P3 Note rather than a Fail.
counterexample: Latent and unmeasured. App S keeps unsent replies server-side per person and conversation, which hireops_rules.md:181 allows. In the hro_messaging session the judge leaves an unsent reply in Noor's Platform Engineer conversation. In the later hro_long_thread session the box opens with that leftover text and the judge types its own unfinished reply. A literal reading of the bar 'the reply still reads exactly what was typed' fails, so hro_long_thread (5.5/61) is lost for correct draft behaviour. App D keeps no drafts, starts with an empty box and can pass that criterion. Separately, no measured reward-ordering run (golden vs mutated weaker apps) exists to confirm the ranking.
suggested_fix: Add the polish prompt's sentence to functional/prompt.md ('If a message or note box already holds text from an earlier review, record it and clear it before typing your own'). Before clearance, record a hash-bound reward-ordering run through the configured verifier, comparing the golden with at least two mutated weaker apps. Do not change scoring.toml or score.py.
